about.metaDescription: Learn about the H-MIP research project, its methods, institutions and public results.
about.title: Research on human–mosquito interaction
about.lead: H-MIP studies how people and mosquitoes meet. This public site presents the project’s questions and methods in a form that residents and local decision makers can explore.

project.title: Understanding exposure in daily life
paragraphs: The Human–Mosquito Interaction Project investigates the circumstances in which people encounter mosquitoes. Its research connects human activity and movement with mosquito ecology, with a focus on the tiger mosquito in Catalonia.
H-MIP Explore is the public-facing companion to that research. Its map presents monthly model estimates for Catalonia. Further survey findings will appear when verified data is available.

methods.title: Several methods, one interaction question
methods.intro: The project draws on complementary sources. Together they can describe both the mosquito side of an encounter and the human activity around it.

steps.title: Interviews
steps.text: Field interviews capture reported bite experiences and their context.

steps.title: Citizen science
steps.text: Public observations, including those made through Mosquito Alert, contribute evidence about mosquitoes.

steps.title: Mobility
steps.text: Movement and activity patterns help frame where encounters may happen.

steps.title: Laboratory analysis
steps.text: Blood-meal analysis can help identify mosquito feeding patterns.

steps.title: Spatial modelling
steps.text: Models bring different evidence together to examine geographic patterns.

steps.title: Uncertainty
steps.text: Research estimates need their limits and uncertainty explained alongside them.

when.metaDescription: Explore the hourly and monthly patterns in reported mosquito bites in Catalonia.
when.title: When bites happen
when.lead: These shares come from reported bites. They do not measure a person's chance of being bitten at a given hour or month.
when.sourceNote: Shares are based on reported bites; intervals are 95% Bayesian credible intervals.
when.scrollHint: Scroll the chart horizontally on small screens.
when.settingIntro: Reports are also grouped by setting. Interval bounds are not available for these two values.

hour.title: Reports concentrate in the evening
hour.takeaway: {value}% of reports fall from {start} to before {end}.
hour.text: This distribution describes the time of reports. It does not isolate mosquito activity from people's exposure or reporting patterns.
hour.chartNote: Bars show the supplied share; lower and upper bounds are listed in the data table.
hour.method: Lower and upper bounds form a 95% credible interval for each share, based on the posterior predictive distribution. The sample size counts bite reports.

month.title: Reports peak in summer
month.text: The monthly distribution describes reported bites, not a population-wide risk estimate.
month.chartNote: Bars show the supplied share; lower and upper bounds are listed in the data table.
month.method: Lower and upper bounds form a 95% credible interval for each share, based on the posterior predictive distribution. The sample size counts bite reports.

activities.metaDescription: Explore reported bite shares by activity, place and season in Catalonia.
activities.title: What are people doing when bites are reported?
activities.lead: Compare the activity and place recorded with each bite report. These shares describe reports, not an individual's risk in each situation.
activities.sourceNote: Shares are based on reported bites; intervals are 95% Bayesian credible intervals.
activities.rateNote: The optional source rate appears only when the dataset supplies it. Check the dataset metadata for its definition and unit.

activity.heading: Activities recorded with bites
activity.takeaway: The leading activity in the selected season accounts for {value}% of reports.
activity.text: A high share may also reflect how long people spend in an activity. It does not establish risk per hour.
activity.method: Lower and upper bounds form a 95% credible interval for each share, based on the posterior predictive distribution. The sample size counts bite reports.

place.heading: Places recorded with bites
place.takeaway: The leading place in the selected season accounts for {value}% of reports.
place.text: Place shares describe reported locations, not mosquito abundance or the risk associated with being in a location.
place.method: Lower and upper bounds form a 95% credible interval for each share, based on the posterior predictive distribution. The sample size counts bite reports.
